content.thinking: Contrast with R-CNN, then the grid, cite b2, b1, b3.

content.text: This sentence is the paper's central move. Earlier detectors such as R-CNN first propose candidate regions and then run a classifier on each one, so detection is a pipeline of separately trained stages [b2]. YOLO instead treats the whole job as one regression: a single network looks at the full image once and directly outputs box coordinates and class probabilities [b1]. Concretely, the image is divided into an S × S grid, and each grid cell predicts B bounding boxes, a confidence score for each box, and C conditional class probabilities [b3]. Because there is only one network evaluation per image, the detector can be optimised end to end and runs in real time.
